Topic 11.2: Water SWIMMING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Water SWIMMING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you feel when SWIMMING Orientation learner should be able to; guided to walk around the walking in water?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WATER SWIMMING
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Water SWIMMING helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116

What this means
In this part you learn to identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water SWIMMING” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Water SWIMMING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Water SWIMMING” around your school. (skill: identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Water SWIMMING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Water SWIMMING from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Water SWIMMING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Water SWIMMING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you feel when SWIMMING Orientation learner should be able to; guided to walk around the walking in water?
2. What do you like most water for safe swimming swimming pool about being in water?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Water SWIMMING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify basic floating • Encourage learners to open techniques for swimming eyes in water confidently 116.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
